statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, r is exactly the sorted list of all prime pairs for n: len(r) is the number of integers x such that 2 <= x <= n - x and both x and n - x are prime; for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), len(r[i]) = 2, writing x_i = r[i][0] and y_i = r[i][1], we have x_i <= y_i, x_i + y_i = n, and x_i and y_i are prime; the first coordinates are strictly increasing with i; and every integer x with 2 <= x <= n - x such that x and n - x are prime occurs as the first coordinate of exactly one entry r[i], with r[i][1] = n - x.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000. The argument is a Std.I64, but it is identified here with its mathematical integer value. Indices are 0-based. An integer z is prime iff z > 1 and the only positive divisors of z are 1 and z.

statement: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 1000000, find_prime_pairs n returns a result r; equivalently, the call does not fail, panic, overflow, or go out of bounds.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, every entry of the outer vector has exactly two coordinates: for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), len(r[i]) = 2.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, every entry of r is a pair [x, y] of integers satisfying 1 <= x <= y <= n.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, every entry of r is a pair [x, y] with x + y = n, using ordinary mathematical integer addition.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, for every entry [x, y] of r, the first coordinate x is prime.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000. An integer z is prime iff z > 1 and its only positive divisors are 1 and z.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, for every entry [x, y] of r, the second coordinate y is prime.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000. An integer z is prime iff z > 1 and its only positive divisors are 1 and z.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, the entries are strictly increasing in their first coordinate: for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), r[i][0] < r[j][0].
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, for every integer x satisfying 2 <= x <= n - x such that x and n - x are both prime, there exists exactly one index i with 0 <= i < len(r) such that r[i][0] = x and r[i][1] = n - x.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000. An integer z is prime iff z > 1 and its only positive divisors are 1 and z.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, the second coordinates are strictly decreasing: for every i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), r[i][1] > r[j][1].
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, len(r) equals the number of integers x such that 2 <= x <= n - x, x is prime, and n - x is prime.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000. An integer z is prime iff z > 1 and its only positive divisors are 1 and z.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, len(r) = 0 if and only if there is no integer x with 2 <= x <= n - x such that both x and n - x are prime.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000. An integer z is prime iff z > 1 and its only positive divisors are 1 and z.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, every entry [x, y] of r has x = 2.
preconditions: n is an odd integer with 1 <= n <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, len(r) = 0.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 3.

statement: Whenever find_prime_pairs n returns a result r, r has exactly one entry, namely r[0][0] = 2 and r[0][1] = 2.
